correctness.rationale: Exact neighborhood-intersection classification proves all three possible triple structures and their necessary-and-sufficient parameter conditions, with constructive traces and obstructions. Pair types follow from distance-one/two common neighbors. Collinear triples are counted as coordinate lines while noncollinear triples have unique centers. A four-support obstruction handles both multi-axis and single-line possibilities, excluding every higher degree. Independent direct-trace code passes fourteen parameter pairs and small four-support checks; no finite extrapolation is used.

originality.rationale: The 2020 original Hamming-edge study (arXiv:2007.16042, Section 4) gives VC dimension/density and common-neighbor intersection lemmas but not the coefficientwise enumeration. The 2024 graph VC-algorithms source does not specialize to the count. Accessible comparison with a prior all-parameter closed-neighborhood census shows that the concept families, triple classes and coefficients differ; at \(H(2,4)\), open and closed counts are 320 and 288. Searches did not reveal an equivalent open-neighborhood complete polynomial. Priority under alternate terminology remains a residual risk.

value.rationale: The exact all-degree support-count polynomial is a natural sharpened invariant beyond the known Hamming open-neighborhood VC dimension. It resolves all d,q with three geometrically distinct maximal-support configurations and sharp q/d thresholds, including explicit counts such as 320 shattered triples in \(H(2,4)\). It is not a mere parameter substitution or a predetermined finite slice; the different multiplicities of collinear versus uniquely centered triples require a structural classification. No downstream application is claimed without evidence.
